Ophthalmology · published research

Retinitis pigmentosa (RP)

Small uncontrolled reports describe short-term visual-acuity or perimetry changes, but electrophysiology findings are mixed and no randomized clinical trial establishes benefit.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Small uncontrolled reports describe short-term visual-acuity or perimetry changes, but electrophysiology findings are mixed and no randomized clinical trial establishes benefit.

Summary of the Evidence

Six publications are listed for retinitis pigmentosa. Five have human evidence, including single-arm, comparison, case-series, and case-report designs; one publication is a rat model, and a mixed human-animal paper also includes mouse experiments. These are publication counts, not necessarily independent patient cohorts. Overlap among small reports from related groups cannot be ruled out. Siqueira et al. 2024

Human and clinical evidence

The 2024 short-term study treated 12 people with multiwavelength PBM and reported possible improvement in visual acuity and fundus automated perimetry, without significant short-term adverse findings. Several other reports are small case reports or case series. A 2022 comparison study of 12 participants reported a mean gain of 5.4 letters at eight weeks, but cone-derived flicker responses were nearly absent and no measurable electroretinographic change was reported. These studies lack robust randomized comparisons, and visual measures may fluctuate in small samples. No publication establishes preservation of vision over the long term.

Animal evidence

One rat study reports preservation of mitochondrial redox state and retinal protection in a model of inherited retinal degeneration. The mixed human-animal publication also includes mouse retinal-dystrophy work. These experiments inform mechanisms but are not clinical efficacy evidence.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No separate in-vitro or ex-vivo clinical evidence was listed for this indication; the laboratory evidence is embedded in the mixed animal publication.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Human protocols include multiwavelength or low-level laser treatments with different schedules and treatment durations. The source records do not establish a standard device, dose, or exposure route. Small samples and short follow-up limit generalization across RP genotypes and disease stages.

Interpretation

The human evidence is exploratory and mainly uncontrolled. Apparent short-term visual changes do not demonstrate disease modification, and retinal electrophysiology findings are not consistent. Independent masked trials with genotype and stage characterization are needed.

Evidence strength in source summaryVisual acuity and field outcomes: Small uncontrolled signal Retinal electrophysiology and durability: Uncertain
Publications and records6 publications: 5 human-tagged reports, including single-arm or comparison studies, case reports, and a case series, plus 2 animal-tagged publications (rat and mouse models), one of which also reports human outcomes.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Five human-tagged reports include case reports, a case series, and small uncontrolled or comparison studies; one paper also includes a mouse model. Short-term visual changes are reported, but controlled evidence is absent and participant overlap between related reports cannot be excluded.

Publication and study types

  • Unique human cohorts are not deduplicated; possible overlap among related small reports remains.
